proposal: The Mandate recommends reforms to how National Ambient Air Quality Standards are set and implemented: have the Clean Air Scientific Advisory Committee weigh all statutory factors, including social and economic effects of attainment strategies; limit requirements on areas redesignated to attainment to what the statute requires; streamline highway conformity showings; guard against use of error-correction authority to push states toward federal plans; limit reliance on the general rulemaking authority in section 301; and, if possible, return standard setting to Congress (pp. 424-425).
remaining: A rule or guidance on how NAAQS are set that directs consideration of attainment and implementation feasibility (p. 424)
Limits on requirements for areas moving from nonattainment to attainment beyond statutory ones (pp. 424-425)
Policies limiting error-correction authority and section 301 rulemaking authority (p. 425)
Any legislative return of standard setting to Congress (p. 425)

status_summary: No EPA rule or guidance on the NAAQS process itself, on the factors the Clean Air Scientific Advisory Committee weighs, on post-attainment requirements, on error correction, or on returning standard setting to Congress was found; a CASAC meeting notice of 2026-07-02 (91 FR 40536) announces only a briefing on the existing review process. On 2026-03-09 the EPA Administrator announced a chair and six members of the committee for 2026 through 2028, including members from two state agencies and several private firms; the announcement does not address the statutory factors the committee considers. On 2026-03-23 EPA finalized a determination that the Phoenix-Mesa ozone area would have met the 2015 standard by its deadline but for international emissions, keeping it Moderate, and on 2026-04-30 it proposed the same type of finding for Utah's Northern Wasatch Front while proposing to repeal a reclassification to Serious; these related actions, together with a 2026-06-12 proposed rule (91 FR 35639) that would remove repeat prior-classification SIP elements for reclassified ozone areas, ease implementation burdens but are not among the listed recommendations.

timeline.event: EPA published a request for nominations to the Clean Air Scientific Advisory Committee, with nominations due 2025-06-02.
The EPA Administrator announced selection of a chair and six members of the Clean Air Scientific Advisory Committee for two-year terms running 2026 through 2028.

EPA finalized a determination that the Phoenix-Mesa area would have attained the 2015 ozone standard by its August 2024 Moderate deadline but for international emissions, keeping its Moderate classification (91 FR 13777).

EPA proposed to repeal the December 2024 reclassification of the Utah Northern Wasatch Front ozone area to Serious and to find attainment by the Moderate date but for international emissions (91 FR 23209; comments due 2026-06-01).

EPA proposes the Ozone Reclassification State Implementation Plan Rule (91 FR 35639, docket EPA-HQ-OAR-2025-0201), which would limit a reclassified ozone area to the Clean Air Act section 182 requirements for its current classification and drop repeat prior-classification SIP elements; comments closed 2026-07-13. Related implementation action, not among the listed recommendations.
EPA noticed a CASAC public meeting for 2026-07-22 to receive a briefing on the NAAQS review process and upcoming review documents (document 2026-13400).

title: Reform NAAQS process: CASAC factors, post-attainment limits, conformity, error correction
uncertainties: The Phoenix-Mesa final rule and the Utah proposal summary were read on federalregister.gov; the Phoenix-Mesa rule shows an effective-date discrepancy (2026-03-23 in its DATES section, 2026-04-22 in its metadata). The 2026-06-12 reclassification proposal was read through its first 100,000 characters. Per a university tracker, EPA asked the D.C. Circuit on 2025-11-24 to vacate the 2024 PM2.5 standard, the court upheld the standard on 2026-06-26, and EPA proposed designations under it on 2026-10-06; this was not confirmed against court records and is not placed in the timeline, and its relationship to the Mandate's process recommendations is unclear. Federal Register API queries (CASAC, international emissions, PM NAAQS) and web searches for a NAAQS process memorandum or CASAC charge change found none. Whether new CASAC members were chosen for viewpoint balance is not assessed. The printed text on pages 424 and 425 does not mention international or background emissions, so the international-emissions findings are a related action rather than a stated element. The committee membership reset itself is credited in c13-05; this record tracks only whether the committee weighs the statutory factors.
